children: Recent Mexican inflation readings show some moderation in upward pressure but aren't comfortable enough, "in particular core and services," for the central bank to consider additional interest-rate cuts, Goldman Sachs's chief Latin America economist Alberto Ramos says in a note. That is even more the case "when taking into consideration recent firmer domestic activity prints, higher oil prices and dollar yields, and the FOMC Fed Funds hike which further narrowed the already thin Mexico-U.S. rate differential," he adds. Inflation in Mexico was 3.42% in mid-September, with core CPI at 3.79%. In its interest-rate decision at 3 p.m. ET, the Bank of Mexico is expected to stay on hold for a third straight time.
